# Bounded capacity approximate broadcasting implies uniform classical reconstruction

9 October 2026 UTC. Complete stitched mathematical argument derived from the audited common-comparator theorem and independently reconstructed reductions. This is internal analytic verification, including separate checks of the comparator, weighted-tracial extension, compatible smoothing, and pair extraction. It is not external peer review, formal proof certification, or a historical-priority claim.

## The statement

An experiment E is any nonempty family of density matrices on one finite-dimensional Hilbert space. Its family need not be finite. Define, with natural-log entropy,

C(E)=sup_(finite priors p on E) {S(Σ_x p_xρ_x)−Σ_x p_x S(ρ_x)},

b₂(E)=inf_(CPTP B:H→H⊗H) sup_(ρ∈E) max_(a=1,2) T(B_aρ,ρ),

e(E)=inf_(entanglement-breaking CPTP Λ:H→H) sup_(ρ∈E) T(Λρ,ρ),

where T(ρ,ν)=||ρ−ν||₁/2 and B_a is the a-th marginal. The infima are over ordinary channels on the entire input matrix algebra, not only on the promised states. A single Λ must work for every member of E.

**Theorem.** For every finite C there exists a dimension- and family-cardinality-independent function f_C:[0,1]→[0,1], with f_C(b)→0 as b↓0, such that

C(E)≤C implies e(E)≤f_C(b₂(E)).

Equivalently, for arbitrary growing-dimensional experiments E_n,

sup_n C(E_n)<∞ and b₂(E_n)→0 imply e(E_n)→0.

The capacity assumption is a supremum over all finite priors. A bound for just one chosen prior is not this hypothesis. No efficient algorithm, uniformly bounded measurement alphabet, diamond-norm approximation of the channel on unrestricted inputs, or finite exact entanglement-breaking power is asserted.

The proof below specifies an explicit, though quantitatively weak, modulus by an infimum over a smoothing tolerance. It therefore proves uniformity rather than merely extracting a subsequence-specific classical channel.

## 1 A common reference and compatible smoothing

Closing E in the compact state space leaves all three quantities unchanged. The continuous entropy graph has compact convex hull in real dimension at most d². Consequently a finite prior attains C(E); let σ be its mean. For every ρ∈E one has D(ρ||σ)≤C(E). # End-to-end adversarial audit of bounded-capacity broadcasting reconstruction

Date: 9 October 2026 UTC.

## Verdict and exact scope

The stitched theorem in `BOUNDED_CAPACITY_BROADCASTING_THEOREM.md` passes this independent end-to-end analytic audit. I found no missing mathematical implication or counterexample under its precise assumptions. The complete composition, not merely its separately named lemmas, gives

C(E_n) uniformly bounded and b₂(E_n)→0 ⇒ e(E_n)→0,

where capacity takes the supremum over all finite priors, broadcasting error is uniform over the entire family and both receivers, and e uses one ordinary full-domain EB channel per experiment. Each ambient Hilbert space is finite dimensional; dimensions and family cardinalities may grow without bound. A family in a given finite dimension may itself be infinite.

This is an internal analytic audit, not external peer review, proof-assistant verification, or historical-priority clearance. No numerical evidence is used. The conclusion does not include infinite-dimensional input spaces, a bounded output alphabet, efficient implementation, diamond-norm approximation, or any unrestricted channel reconstruction theorem.

## Material independently read

- The complete stitched theorem, 194 lines at audit time.
- The complete pinned smoothing audit `sources/d-b4ddaa96b233287d.txt`, and its independent contemporary reconstruction `CAPACITY_SMOOTHING_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`.
- The complete centralization/Petz source `sources/d-c851b6e4ba719edf.txt`, including all of its Sections 1–10 and its deliberately open historical remainder.
- The complete pair-extraction audit `N46_PAIR_BROADCAST_GAP_AUDIT.md`.
- The C4 source and independent covariance reconstruction in `../c4_audit/`, and the weighted extension and cross-check.
- Primary quantum-substate theorem: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1103.6067, Theorem 1 and fidelity convention, independently reopened. The squared-fidelity convention and factor (1−η)⁻¹2^(D_obs/η) match the smoother's constants; D_obs_bits≤D_rel_bits+1 yields its nats conversion.
- Primary Rényi-DPI source https://arxiv.org/pdf/1306.5920 independently reopened. Alpha two is within the DPI range required here.

The older sources' statements that the broad gate remains open are historical statements about the absence of the final common comparator there. They are neither hypotheses nor counterarguments
